findings.reason: §20's done-when ("every reader reads the rolled set, returning every row exactly once") is unachievable through the search the section itself prescribes, so the census must be stated as a search over path-taking call sites and the reader rewritten in the same node.
findings.text: §20 states it "finds every reader with a search for `RECEIPTS_FILENAME` and `requests.jsonl`", but the reader at `receipt_bins.py:82` (`read_receipt_rows`) takes the receipts path as an argument and does `Path(receipts_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")`, naming neither string, so that search returns only the producer (`request_receipts.py:43`), the router (`router.py:1750`) and the CLI path builder (`cli.py:2648`) and misses this one; its caller `collect_receipt_bins` (`receipt_bins.py:100`), its test `tests/test_agent_receipt_bins.py:41`, and `cache_estimate.py:38` (which §20 lists as a write target but which only imports `STATUS_COMPLETED`) sit in the same blind spot — the same shape also hides §21's third reader, since `serving_receipts.py:554` (`tier_paths`) and `telemetry_retention.py:317` (`raw_receipt_files`) reach the raw file by glob and by derived path rather than by a constant

findings.reason: the node cannot be cut from the section as written, because the watermark's home and the treatment of the trailing partial bucket are the section's substance and neither is stated.
findings.text: §21 requires "compaction reads only rows it has not yet compacted", dictates that "output must stay byte-identical to a full recompaction", and names no owner for the watermark that says which rows are compacted, while the three files it writes (`serving_receipts.py`, `telemetry_store.py`, `telemetry_retention.py`) and the recorder's restart path each need it; the two constraints also conflict at the boundary of a live window, because the minute and hour bucket covering the current instant is incomplete when it is written and an append-only compactor cannot correct its tail to the full-recompaction form that `tests/test_telemetry_store.py` demands

findings.reason: the plan must either extend the tier naming owner to carry the day (one ladder, day-stamped segments) or state the per-day pairing in §21 and §22, and the current text leaves the choice to the implementing node.
findings.text: §21 rolls the raw record at each UTC midnight and says only that "the naming must keep three readers working"; `tier_paths` derives the minute and hour tier names from the raw file's stem (`path.name[: -len(suffix)]`), so a per-day raw name forks the tier ladder into one `.minute`/`.hour` pair per day instead of the single ladder the owner documents ("one receipts directory holds a serve's whole retention ladder", `serving_receipts.py:557`), and §22's tier-equality retirement and five-week minute-tier ageing then have to pair each day's raw against its own tiers, a rule §22 does not state and `telemetry_retention.is_raw_receipt` (`telemetry_retention.py:302`) does not implement for a name that carries both a job id and a date

findings.reason: the section must account for the public surface it adds in its own text, which is a one-line addition naming the retired or unchanged reader and why no merge is possible.
findings.text: with public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0 and refusal_families 0, §17 adds one public definition, the reader `rate_in_force(history, slug, when)` ("the module exposes one reader"), and no scoped section names what it retires or merges or states why nothing can be retired

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §21 asks the recorder, the compactor and the retention scan to share an incremental "rows not yet compacted" watermark, requires append-only output to stay byte-identical to a full recompaction, and names no owner for that watermark nor how a partially-elapsed window is corrected.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §21 rolls the raw serve record to a per-day name while the tier ladder is derived from the raw file's stem, so placement of the tiers is forked from its owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §17 adds `rate_in_force` to a module's public surface and no scoped section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan does search the codebase and its two reuse claims verify (the index's `(host, boot_id, path, inode)` tail keying is real at `imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:246` and `:264`, and the `requests-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` name shape is already described at `imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_retention.py:22` and `:308`), but §20's prescribed census method (a search for `RECEIPTS_FILENAME` and `requests.jsonl` literals) cannot find the reader that takes the receipts path as an argument.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every scoped change is an extension of the module that already owns the behaviour (`provider_prices` gains the history beside the table it writes, `watch.period_row` is extended rather than wrapped, the generated serve command gains a flag its engine already publishes, the receipt sink and recorder gain a roll), and no new parallel layer over existing machinery is proposed.
